message.content:
**Decision: Buy — order filled.**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and found a business that is growing modestly but very profitably: total net sales of $391.0B (up 2% from $383.3B), operating income of $123.2B, net income of $93.7B, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.3B, with gross margin expanding to 46.2% on a 13% increase in high-margin Services revenue ($96.2B) and $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. Net income and EPS were slightly below FY2023 ($97.0B / $6.13) solely because of a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not an operating deterioration — operating income actually rose from $114.3B. Offsetting considerations I weighed were the 8% decline in Greater China sales, flat iPhone revenue, and ongoing DOJ/DMA antitrust and App Store regulatory pressure. On balance the durable cash generation, margin expansion, and the fact that the earnings dip is a non-recurring tax item justified a position, so within your mandate (AAPL only, buy only, ≤$10,000 per order, ≤$20,000 total today, limit near market, no withdrawals) I placed a single limit buy of 40 shares of AAPL at $223.00 against a quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), a notional of about $8,920 — under the per-order cap and leaving the $50,000 cash balance and existing 100 MSFT shares untouched. The order filled at $223.00.
